title: REST Feasibility Study: A Trial of Lemborexant for Sleep Problems After Mild Traumatic Brain Injury
official: REST Feasibility Study: Recovery and Evaluation of Sleep After Mild Traumatic Brain Injury. A Double-Blind, Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Feasibility Trial of Lemborexant
summary:
The goal of this feasibility study is to learn if a larger trial testing lemborexant (Dayvigo) for insomnia after concussion can be carried out successfully. It will enrol adults aged 18 to 65 who have trouble sleeping after a mild traumatic brain injury/concussion in the past 12 months. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Can enough participants be recruited each month?
* Do participants stay in the study through the end of treatment (4 weeks) and follow-up (8 weeks)?
* Do participants take the study capsules as prescribed?
* Do participants complete the study questionnaires and wear a home sleep headband as planned?

Researchers will compare lemborexant plus sleep hygiene education to a placebo (a look-alike capsule with no medication) plus sleep hygiene education. The study will get early estimates of any differences in sleep quality, concussion symptoms, mood, anxiety, quality of life, and side effects, to help plan a larger trial.

Participants will:

* Complete a screening phone call and an in-person baseline visit in Halifax
* Take one capsule (lemborexant 5 mg or placebo) every night for 4 weeks from a blister pack, and receive a sleep hygiene handout
* Wear an EEG headband at home to record their sleep for the first 5 nights and last 5 nights of treatment
* Receive a weekly phone call during treatment to check on side effects
* Attend a visit at Week 4 to return the headband and blister packs
* Complete questionnaires online at the start, at Week 4, and at a Week 8 phone follow-up
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) within the preceding 12 months per 2023 ACRM criteria, confirmed by structured interview using a standardized checklist; suspected mTBI and mTBI with neuroimaging evidence of intracranial injury are eligible
* Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) greater than or equal to 8 at pre-screen and baseline
* If using SSRI/SNRI, must be taking for greater than or equal to 1 month prior to starting the study
* Access to a smart device (ie. tablet or smartphone)

Exclusion Criteria:

* Previous moderate/severe TBI
* Current use of carbamazepine or phenytoin or moderate/strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or inducers
* Diagnosis of narcolepsy
* Current use of sedating medications (melatonin, z-drugs, benzodiazepines, sedating antidepressants or antipsychotics)
* Active substance use disorder
* Diagnosis of liver disease or COPD
* Active pregnancy or any participants of childbearing potential who are unwilling to use contraception from consent until 7 days after the final dose of study medication
* Active suicidal ideation.
